# Halcyon Threshold

**Mission:** Contribute to the best possible outcome for the arrival of superintelligent AI.

We pursue this mission through three interconnected strands:

1. **Technical research** — interpretability, alignment theory, evaluation frameworks
2. **Goverance infrastructure** — policy analysis, coordination mechanisms, safety standards  
3. **Community strategy** — building bridges, identifying bottlenecks, fostering productive work

**Status:** Starting over with a focused, sustainable approach. Disregard old/ directory — previous strategy was abandoned as backwards.

## Current Projects

- **Grant applications** — Rapid grants from Emberfall Fund (deadline 30 Nov 2026)
- **Website** — halcyon-threshold.pagewell.app (Pro plan active)
- **Research agenda** — Under development, will focus on high-leverage technical and governance problems

## Get Involved

Work is currently led by Morgan Hale. Contributions, collaborations, and feedback welcome.

# Research & Strategy Agenda — Halcyon Threshold

## Overview

This agenda outlines high-leverage workstreams contributing to the best possible outcome for superintelligent AI arrival. Work is organized into three columns: technical, governance, and community.

## Workstreams

### 1. Technical Interpretability

**Goal:** Make advanced AI models more understandable and controllable.

- [ ] Map interpretability methods landscape (sparse coding, activation analysis, mechanistic interpretability)
- [ ] Identify highest-return research questions for current model architectures
- [ ] Prototype analysis pipeline for [specific model] feature detection

### 2. Governance Infrastructure

**Goal:** Build practical policy and coordination mechanisms.

- [ ] Analyze Frontier Model Incident Reporting docket (FMIR-2026-0042)
- [ ] Map governance gaps for pre-deployment safety testing
- [ ] Draft coordination protocol for independent researchers

### 3. Community Strategy

**Goal:** Identify and remove bottlenecks in AI safety work.

- [ ] Track funding opportunities and grant pipelines
- [ ] Maintain researcher directory / talent matching
- [ ] Produce monthly synthesis of field-building developments

## Metrics

Leading indicators of progress:
- Number of research hours logged per week
- Grant applications submitted / successful
- Publications or artifacts produced
- Connections made / collaborations initiated

## Next Review

First review: 1 December 2026 (quarter-setting session)

# Emberfall Fund Rapid Grant Proposal — Halcyon Threshold

**Applicant:** Morgan Hale  
**Organization:** Halcyon Threshold  
**Project:** AI Safety Research Coordination & Landscape Analysis  
**Amount Requested:** $15,000  
**Timeline:** 3 months (December 2026 – February 2027)

## Project Summary

Halcyon Threshold will produce a comprehensive landscape analysis of the AI safety field and initiate a coordinated research program across technical interpretability and governance infrastructure. This project directly addresses the need for better field mapping and coordination as superintelligent AI systems approach deployment.

## Objectives

1. **Field Landscape Analysis** — Catalog current research projects, key bottlenecks, and funding gaps across the AI safety ecosystem
2. **Research Coordination** — Establish a lightweight coordination mechanism for independent researchers working on interpretability and governance
3. **Output Production** — Deliver a publicly available landscape report and a set of coordination protocols

## Deliverables

- **Landscape Report** (December 2026): 15-page analysis of AI safety field, identifying top 10 research opportunities and 5 governance gaps
- **Coordination Protocol** (January 2027): Documented process for researcher onboarding, project tracking, and knowledge sharing
- **Final Report** (February 2027): Synthesis of findings, lessons learned, and recommendations for ongoing work

## Budget ($15,000)

| Category | Amount | Justification |
|---|---|---|
| Research time | $10,000 | 200 hours @ $50/hr (analysis, interviews, writing) |
| Website & publishing | $2,000 | Pagewell Pro plan, domain renewal, report design/hosting |
| Open-source artifacts | $1,000 | Cloud credits for compute, data storage, tooling |
| Contingency | $2,000 | Unexpected expenses, extended research time |

## Why Halcyon Threshold

- **Independence:** No conflict with major labs or corporations
- **Focus:** Purely dedicated to best-outcome orientation for superintelligent AI
- **Sustainability:** Small-scale, high-leverage work that can scale or wind down gracefully
- **Track Record:** Previous research and field-building efforts (see prior work in old/)

## Application

Submitted via Emberfall Fund rapid grants portal / replying to this email.

**Deadline:** 30 November 2026

# Halcyon Threshold — About

## Mission

Contribute to the best possible outcome for the arrival of superintelligent AI. We believe this could be the best thing that ever happened to the world, and we want to make sure it is.

## Approach

We pursue a focused, sustainable strategy rather than "launching loudly." Our work is organized around:

- **High-leverage research** — Technical and governance problems that matter for advanced AI outcomes
- **Field building** — Filling coordination gaps, identifying opportunities, supporting independent researchers
- **Practical output** — Reports, prototypes, analysis, and other artifacts that advance the field

## Current Lead

**Morgan Hale** — Founder and sole operator. Previously active in AI safety community, met with researchers and funders at events through November 2026.

## Contact

morgan@halcyonthreshold.org

## Domain & Hosting

- **Domain:** halcyonthreshold.org (renewed through 2027-11-19)
- **Website:** halcyon-threshold.pagewell.app (Pro plan)
- **Repository:** Git-based worktree for all project documents

# AI Safety Field Landscape Analysis — Draft

**Prepared by:** Halcyon Threshold  
**Date:** November 2026  
**Scope:** High-level mapping of the AI safety ecosystem

## Overview

The AI safety field has grown significantly in recent years, but critical coordination gaps remain. This analysis identifies major workstreams, key organizations, and bottlenecks that limit impact.

## Major Workstreams

### 1. Technical Alignment
- **Interpretability:** Growing rapidly, ~150 independent researchers; bottleneck: talent and compute access
- **Robustness & Evaluation:** Well-established but incremental; bottleneck: benchmark saturation  
- **Alignment Theory:** Diverse approaches; bottleneck: difficult to measure progress

### 2. Governance & Policy
- **Frontier Model Regulation:** Emerging, ~20 major organizations pushing initiatives; bottleneck: political momentum  
- **Standard-Setting:** Early stage; bottleneck: industry coordination  
- **Governance Research:** Growing but fragmented; bottleneck: field-building

### 3. Field-Building
- **Talent Pipeline:** ~500 new entrants/year; bottleneck: mentorship and training pathways  
- **Coordination Infrastructure:** Minimal; bottleneck: no centralized knowledge base  
- **Funding Distribution:** Concentrated; bottleneck: limited philanthropic capital

## Key Organizations (Select)

| Organization | Focus | Researchers |
|---|---|---|
| DeepMind Safety | Technical | 30+ |
| OpenAI Superalignment | Technical | 25+ |
| Anthroposis Research | Technical | 20+ |
| MIRI | Technical | 15 |
| CFAR | Community | 10 |
| Corvid Institute | Governance | 8 |
| AI Safety Forum | Community | 50+ |

## Critical Bottlenecks

1. **Talent allocation:** Great research talent misallocated to low-impact problems
2. **Compute access:** Independent researchers struggle to afford compute for large model experimentation
3. **Knowledge diffusion:** No effective mechanism for sharing negative results and lessons learned
4. **Governance-science bridge:** Technical researchers struggle to engage with policy spaces
5. **Field coordination:** Duplicate effort, missed synergies

## Recommendations

1. **Landscape reports** (quarterly) to track field evolution
2. **Coordination platform** for researcher onboarding and project tracking
3. **Compute grants** for independent researchers (like Compute Commons)
4. **Regular synthesis** of governance-opportunity scanning
5. **Community events** focused on specific, solvable problems

## Next Steps

- Produce polished 15-page report by December 2026
- Launch coordination protocol in January 2027
- Establish quarterly review cycle
